object_description: connected school and sports buildings with courtyard pavilion
design_condition: The composition follows the district morphology, places the main volumes along the perimeter, and creates a spacious courtyard with differentiated public and private access.

positive.statement: The urban structure translates the district morphology into plausible streets, courtyards, and alleyways.
The division into a lower movement level and an upper lounge level is functionally convincing through clear visual references and connecting greenery.
The entrance sequence creates a clear address and a passage that can serve both neighbourhood and school use.
The supporting structure impresses with efficient skeleton construction and clear load transfer.
The spatial proposal for the school combines different dimensions coherently and achieves good space and light qualities.
The classrooms are conveniently oriented and the easy access provides good orientation.

negative.statement: The rear courtyard is too complex for the needs of the school.
The public accessibility of the courtyard buildings is problematic from an operational perspective.
The central corridor limits the flexibility of the multi-purpose and lounge areas.
The architectural dominance of the gymnasium head is only partly compatible with its pragmatic use.
The separate exhibition and plant building is architecturally alien and economically unsustainable.
The large floor area and volume result in poor overall economic efficiency.
The facade is comparatively expensive to build, despite positive maintenance and longevity qualities.
